title: Traffic decay protocols for active-passive DR and automated restore sanity
creator: Alyssa Chen
description: Motivation: We need a deterministic, repeatable way to rehearse active->passive failovers that stresses SLO gating, circuit breakers, and load-shedding tiers while validating backup/restore integrity. Current drills tend to be binary (cut all traffic) and don't exercise the gradual pressure, KV reconciliation, or canary gating we rely on in production. This ticket implements a 'traffic decay' protocol: progressively divert traffic away from primary to passive over staged windows, exercising circuit breaker thresholds, load-shedding policies, and automated snapshot/restore validation hooks.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A documented traffic-decay runbook is published in Confluence with clear thresholds and roles.
2) A synthetic drill can be executed end-to-end in test region (eu-west-2-staging) with automated assertions for SLOs, circuit-breaker state transitions, and KV consistency.
3) Restore verification harness runs after each failover stage confirming snapshot checksums, WAL application completeness, and user-visible read/write smoke tests.
4) Post-drill audit shows no unnoticed token-store drift or missing telemetry.
5) Observability dashboards capture stepwise SLO burn and rollback decisions for later analysis.
runbook_outline:
1) Pre-checks: confirm backup age < 10m, active region SLO headroom > configured baseline, ensure runbook channel is open and on-call is paged.
2) Stage 0 (Canary, 60s): route 2% traffic to passive region; monitor 30s windows for increased tail latency or error spikes.
3) Stage 1 (Decay 10m): reduce primary traffic by 25% increments every 2 minutes while enabling tiered load-shedding (L1-L3).
4) Stage 2 (Circuit breaker exercise): intentionally trigger a synthetic latency injection to force circuit-breaker checks and validate automatic reroutes.
5) Stage 3 (Snapshot restore validation): take passive snapshot, run restore harness, verify checksums and KV reconciliation; run smoke tests.
6) Stage 4 (Full switch or rollback): based on gating policies (SLOs, error budget, operator decision) either promote passive or rehydrate primary and revert routing.
7) Post-mortem checklist: collect traces, attach run logs, update playbook artifacts and retro notes.
test_plan:
- Use traffic generator (github.com/redwood/relay-loadgen PR#438) to produce realistic seq-len and query-mix.
- Create synthetic users to exercise caching and KV access patterns.
- Monitor: p50/p95/p99 latency, error_rate, token_costs, KV reconciliation time.
- Assert restore harness returns status OK and checksum match for at least 99.999% of keys.
- Failure injection: add a 500ms server-side processing delay for 15s in Stage 2 to validate circuit-breaker transition and fallback behavior.
- Run the drill with both warm-passive and cold-passive profiles to validate both restore flows.
rollback_plan:
- If SLO burn > configured threshold OR circuit-breaker fails to close within timeout, immediately revert routing to prior snapshot by using routing-conductor run_id and fast-path playbooks.
- Begin active rehydrate: attach WAL stream from passive to primary, verify WAL offset parity, resume traffic only after KV reconciliation AND smoke tests pass.
- If WAL replay stalls, open urgent incident and escalate to infra on-call.
- All rollback steps must be performed in <30 minutes for customer-impacting incidents; otherwise escalate to exec incident process.
notes:
Design decisions made: we intentionally avoid a single large cutover to exercise graceful degradation and economic throttling strategies used by production traffic. The restore harness is extended to include an application-layer smoke test that verifies both read and write path semantics (not just blob checksums). We will reuse existing snapshot tooling (ENG-24001) and extend recovery probes from ENG-41209.
Open questions: how to simulate upstream client backpressure in a non-invasive way; whether to include an opt-in customer traffic cohort for later drills.
